prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 1 "Filling valve (internal frost-burst fitting)": indemnified in all 2 earlier cases; when indemnified t per pc about 52 (80% range 41 to 68); revealed per pc: 48-55 (case 16*), 51-54 (case 25) (* = other policy wording)
- line 2 "Connection hose": indemnified in all 2 earlier cases; when indemnified t per pc about 27 (80% range 21 to 37); revealed per pc: 27-33 (case 16*), 26-28 (case 25) (* = other policy wording)
- line 3 "Senior installer hours": indemnified in all 2 earlier cases; when indemnified t per hr about 98 (80% range 76 to 127); revealed per hr: >=91 (case 16*), >=93 (case 25) (* = other policy wording), so this line (3 hr) about 295 (229 to 382)
- line 4 "Auxiliary and cleaning material": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 2 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 5 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 9 of 21 earlier cases, t = 0 in 12; when indemnified t per pc about 67 (80% range 38 to 97); revealed per pc: >=76 (case 21*), >=76 (case 21*), >=76 (case 21*), 34-45 (case 23*), >=74 (case 27*), 38-44 (case 25) (* = other policy wording)
- line 6 "Thermal imaging camera (leak detection)": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 2 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 7 "Vehicle costs – return visit": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 3 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 9 "Base plaster": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 2 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 10 "Newly plastered substrate": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 2 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 11 "Priming": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 2 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 13 "Facade paint (4 coats)": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 2 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 14 "Painter hours": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 2 earlier cases; no price evidence
- line 18 "Administrative flat rate": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 3 earlier cases; no price evidence

items.rationale: Sections 2.4.4 and 7.1.9 cover like-for-like renewal of the internal frost-fractured valve; Case 25 supports €52 gross.
Section 7.1.9 covers connection elements that must be renewed with the valve; Case 25 supports €27 gross.
Sections 7.1.7(f) and 7.1.9 cover necessary fitting-repair labour; three hours at about €98 gross per hour give approximately €295.

Sections 7.1.7(e) and 7.1.9 cover consumables actually used in the repair, but §3.6(c) excludes the contractor's own small equipment. This generic line was not paid in the reference cases; allow about €7 if actual repair consumables are substantiated.
Sections 7.1.9 and 7.1.11 allow one attendance for covered work; the same-wording Case 25 supports €41 gross.
Sections 2.4.6 and 5.2.2 expressly cover imaging equipment used to locate the escape. Allow €25 for equipment use, consistent with Case 25's upper bound and well within the €2,500 gross event cap.
Section 7.1.11 excludes a separate return attendance unless approved in advance, and none is reported. If approval is evidenced, the initial attendance provides a €41 benchmark.
The facade frost endorsement activates §2.6.2, which covers stripping failed plaster from the damaged area. Allow about €65 per billed unit, or €130 gross for two, excluding separate disposal.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d) cover like-for-like base plaster on the damaged area. Allow €70 gross for the base material without duplicating substrate work or separately billed labour.

Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(c) cover necessary substrate reinstatement on the damaged area. Allow €145 gross for distinct substrate work, without duplicating the base plaster or separately billed painter hours.
Section 2.6.2 covers priming of the repaired area; allow €40 gross for an ordinary primer application, excluding separately billed labour.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(c) cover drying only if needed before reinstatement. Allow €95 gross for a modest drying measure if its necessity and cost are substantiated.

Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(d) cover the coats required by the like-for-like finish system, not extra coats or paint for the rear. Allow €110 gross for paint on the damaged area, with labour priced separately.
Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.7(f) cover labour on the frost-damaged area, not on the separately billed rear elevation. Five hours at about €65 gross give €325.

Sections 2.6.2 and 7.1.8 cover necessary scaffold hire, erection and dismantling; no rear-work apportionment is needed because the scaffold was struck before that work. Roughly 50 m² at €14 gross per m² gives €700.
Sections 2.6.3(a), 7.1.5 and 7.1.6 exclude repainting a separate undamaged elevation, even for colour matching. The €750 figure is a conditional price only, not an allowance.
Sections 2.6.2 and 5.2.2 cover disposal of plaster removed from the insured frost-damaged area. A few rubble sacks support €55 gross for transport and disposal, not a skip charge.
Sections 3.6(b) and 7.1.12 exclude an administrative surcharge that prices no repair work. The €10 figure is a conditional price only, not an allowance.
Section 3.6(a) excludes crew subsistence even on insured work. The €18 figure for three portions is a conditional price only, not an allowance.
